purpose: Art selection previews; not runtime screenshots or exported assets

variants.title: A · 简洁霓虹科技
variants.prompt: Edit the supplied screenshot into a polished but faithful in-game art-direction preview for Portal Hop, an original 2D side-view geometric platform game. Preserve the exact 16:9 camera, navy #131B2B background and faint vertical grid, all platform and wall positions and sizes, pale portal-compatible strips, and the small yellow robot with dark visor, cyan eyes and hand-held gun at exactly the same place and scale. This is a selection preview, not new level design. Remove ALL typography and HUD: the entire top row, top instructions, BLUE FLOOR label, hint circle and red aiming crosshair. Leave the top empty navy background. Only redesign TWO objects: (1) a clearly visible mint-green starting flag on a small pedestal on the LEFT part of the robot's starting platform, just left of the robot, with its own pole and flag silhouette; (2) the mint-green finish gate replacing the existing hollow green rectangle on the middle raised platform. Keep both compact and appropriate to the existing robot scale; the finish gate should be around 1.6 times the robot's height, not a huge portal. Gate openings must stay unobstructed. Avoid changing any other object, adding characters, text, terrain, user-interface panels, copyrighted game imagery or decorative scenery. Show a complete uncluttered game frame, sharp clean 2D artwork with limited shading, not a 3D perspective render. Art direction A: restrained neon minimalism. Starting flag: thin charcoal pole, subtle illuminated mint edge, a crisp elegant pennant with a very slight fabric fold, a small low hexagonal dark pedestal with one mint indicator. Finish gate: sleek charcoal rounded-rectangle frame, thin continuous mint light strips embedded along its sides and top, softly glowing threshold and a few tiny mint particles inside a clean dark opening. Refined and readable at small scale; use mint #55E0AE, charcoal and pale cool grey, keep bloom delicate. The start flag and finish gate should clearly feel like the same visual family.
